record.paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
record.original_question: For an algebraic Anosov action of R^k or Z^k, k ≥ 2, on a biquotient M of a connected Lie group G, and for an ergodic probability Borel measure μ on M, must either μ be a finite sum of measures constructed from Haar measures on closed subgroups of G, or must supp μ fiber equivariantly over a manifold N on which the action reduces to rank one?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 8 (A. Katok, R. Spatzier [128]) . Let M be a manifold which is a biquotient of a connected Lie group G. Given an algebraic Ano sov action of Rk or Zk , k ≥ 2, on M and an ergodic probability Borel measure µ on M , one of the following holds: (i) The measure µ is a ﬁnite sum of measures constructed from Haar measures supported on closed subgroups of G. (ii) The support of µ ﬁbers over a manifold N in an equivariant way such that the action on N reduces to a rank one action.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a connected Lie group and let $M$ be a biquotient of $G$, i.e. $M = A\backslash G / B$ where $A,B$ are closed subgroups of $G$ acting freely and properly on $G$ by left and right translations respectively. An action of $\mathbb{R}^k$ or $\mathbb{Z}^k$ on $M$ is called algebraic if it is induced (via the biquotient construction) by translations of $G$ coming from a homomorphism into $G$. Such an action is called Anosov if some element of $\mathbb{R}^k$ (resp. $\mathbb{Z}^k$) acts as an Anosov diffeomorphism/flow on $M$. Assume $k \ge 2$, and let $\mu$ be an ergodic invariant Borel probability measure on $M$ for the action.

Prove or disprove: at least one of the following must hold.
(i) $\mu$ is a finite sum (convex combination) of measures each of which is constructed from a Haar measure supported on a closed subgroup of $G$ (i.e., $\mu$ is "algebraic").
(ii) The support of $\mu$ fibers equivariantly over a manifold $N$ in such a way that the induced action on $N$ reduces to a rank-one action (i.e., factors through a homomorphism $\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{Z}^k\to\mathbb{Z}$).
artifact.category_tag: measure rigidity for higher-rank abelian actions
artifact.status_search_result: The Katok–Spatzier measure rigidity conjecture remains open in full generality. Substantial partial results are known: measure rigidity has been established in many cases under additional hypotheses (e.g., totally non-symplectic Cartan actions, presence of positive entropy elements, actions on tori and nilmanifolds via work of Einsiedler–Katok–Lindenstrauss, Kalinin–Spatzier, Rodriguez Hertz, Kalinin–Katok, and others), but the general biquotient case has not been resolved.

status_evidence.title: An Invitation to Rigidity Theory (R. J. Spatzier)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys the state of measure and differentiable rigidity conjectures for higher rank abelian actions, indicating partial results and that the full conjecture remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture has many partial results but is not resolved in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Dynamics and Related Fields (A. Gorodnik)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the Katok–Spatzier conjecture on ergodic invariant measures for algebraic Anosov R^k/Z^k actions on biquotients as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: The Katok-Spatzier Conjecture and Generalized Symmetries
status_evidence.snippet: Work toward the Katok–Spatzier conjecture under additional assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Progress under additional hypotheses, not a full resolution.
